title: Private Deployment: Blue-Green Upgrade Flow with Pull-Through Egress Proxy & Image Validation
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD-style ticket specifying an auditable blue-green upgrade flow tailored for Private/VPC customers that restrict outbound network egress. Focus: allow upgrades with minimal operator intervention while preserving air-gap constraints via a pull-through egress proxy, signed release artifacts, and automated validation. This ticket clarifies requirements, acceptance criteria, and operational playbook for ship teams and solutions engineers.
background: Customers in high-regulation environments request predictable zero-risk upgrades for Private deployments where direct access to public registries is blocked. Current upgrade docs assume network egress to multiple endpoints or rely on manual offline bundles. We need a repeatable flow that supports two customer classes: (A) restricted egress with a single customer-managed pull-through proxy/cache, and (B) fully air-gapped sites that accept signed offline bundles. This ticket defines the blue-green orchestration and the verification gates required by Console and operator tooling.
goals: Define a blue-green control-plane upgrade flow that requires no unrestricted outbound egress beyond configured pull-through proxies or allowlisted artifact mirrors
Specify artifact signing and attestation checks (OCI signatures + SBOM) that the private cluster enforces before deploying new images
Define automated canary and roll-forward/rollback acceptance tests (functional + quality + performance) that run inside the customer VPC
Provide an operational playbook for Solutions/SEs to perform an offline upgrade using a signed bundle when the customer is fully air-gapped
Surface upgrade state, validation metrics, and audit events in Redwood Console for private deployments
non_goals: Designing custom customer-side proxy software (we will require standard pull-through registry solutions or supported vendor configs)
Support for arbitrary, ad-hoc unverified artifacts (all images must be signed and meet SBOM/CVE gating)
Replacing customer change-control processes—this ticket augments, not replaces, their change approvals
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Upgrade can execute in a Private VPC that only allows egress to a single configured pull-through mirror. No other outbound endpoints required for image/artifact retrieval.

AC-2: All runtime images and Kubernetes manifests deployed by the upgrade are cryptographically signed (cosign or equivalent). Cluster nodes validate signatures before starting new pods; validation failure aborts the deploy and records audit event.

AC-3: For air-gapped customers, Solutions Engineering can generate a signed offline bundle (release artifacts + manifests + attestation) that is verifiable by the cluster using embedded public key; bundle applies successfully and upgrade completes following the same verification gates as the online flow.

AC-4: Blue-green cutover maintains availability: 99th-percentile inference latency degradation during cutover is <= 10% compared to pre-upgrade baseline, and error rate increase remains < 0.5 percentage points measured across a 30-minute window after cutover for production traffic routed through the customer LB.

AC-5: Canary validation runs a configurable golden prompt set and a set of health checks inside the private network. If the model outputs deviate beyond configured thresholds (n-gram diffs, hallucination rate, or API contract regressions), the system automatically halts the roll and marks a failed canary with diagnostic data surfaced in Console.

AC-6: KV cache warm-up procedure is defined: during blue-green pre-warm phase, we replicate expected recent prefixes to new nodes via secure internal APIs; cache hit-rate for the first 5 minutes after cutover must be >= 60% of baseline for traffic patterns typical of the customer (or fallback to configured cold-start SLO behavior).

AC-7: Upgrade audit trail is produced and visible in Console: artifact hashes, signature verification results, canary test outputs, operator who initiated the upgrade, timestamps, and roll/rollback events.

AC-8: Rollback achieves functional restore to previous version within a customer-configurable SLA (default 15 minutes) and preserves existing inference sessions where possible (graceful draining for replaced pods).

AC-9: Documented whitelisting guide for network teams describing minimal endpoints and ports required for (a) pull-through registry operation, (b) telemetry and license checks (if enabled), and (c) options for fully offline installs.
rollout_plan: 1) Pre-check: verify customer's pull-through mirror config and reachable endpoints via operator-run connectivity tests. 2) Upload signed release metadata to the customer's control plane or prepare offline bundle. 3) Create 'green' environment (new deployment objects pinned to signed images) and run pre-warm tasks (KV cache warm, model weights preload). 4) Execute canary stage: small traffic percentage routed to green and run golden prompts + perf probes. 5) If canary passes, progress progressive traffic shift to green, monitoring thresholds; otherwise abort and rollback. 6) After stable window, decommission blue, rotate tokens/secrets if required, and emit completion audit event. 7) For air-gapped: same steps but artifact acquisition uses local bundle; upload and validation step replaces pull-through fetch.
test_plan: Operator integration test in private staging environment that simulates blocked egress and uses a local pull-through cache
Automated canary suite executing golden prompt diff checks and regression detectors inside the VPC
Performance regression test measuring 95th/99th latency during cutover under synthetic traffic profiles
Air-gap bundle round-trip test: generate bundle -> customer imports bundle -> cluster verifies signatures -> executes upgrade -> validates post-upgrade metrics
Security test: tamper the bundle or manifest to ensure signature verification rejects modifications and records an audit event
notes: Trade-offs: blue-green requires double capacity during the migration window; for customers with constrained capacity we provide a staggered canary + rolling option documented separately. We recommend cosign + Rekor for signature transparency. Solutions must validate that customer pull-through mirrors rewrite image names as expected. Follow-up tickets: automated mirror validation tool (ENG follow-up) and Console UI for offline-bundle generation.
